steps.shell: python3 docs/guide/recipes/09-grip.py --path Box --kind scale-ball --axis x --mod ctrl --dx 80 --dy 4

items.check: Four controlled handle clips on one grey part, with the Part inspector in frame: Scale drag (Size X 4 -> 5), Ctrl+Scale (4 -> 6, centre fixed), Move arrow (Position X -14 -> -13), Rotate ring (Orientation X -45 deg / 0.785 rad).
items.notes: Current build makes new parts solid Medium Stone Grey. docs/guide/recipes/09-grip.py computes each Roblox handle from the part's AABB/camera, so the handle is grabbed even when the frame helper's centring drifts: Scale +X ball dragged 80 px (4 -> 5 m), Ctrl+Scale 80 px (4 -> 6 m, centre fixed), Move +X arrow 80 px (1 m = one grid step), Rotate X ring 60 px (-45 deg). Each drag is followed by Ctrl+Z so the next clip starts from size 4 at position -14. The record rect keeps the viewport and the Part inspector's Transform fields, so the numeric readout (Size/Position/Orientation) is visible; the helper holds the button for 1.5 s and the clip waits 3 s before stopping so the slow editor rebuild lands inside the recording.

The current build paints new parts solid Medium Stone Grey, so the wall now matches the shipped greybox (the old media was the pre-fix orange).
